items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Johnny Mitchel, Burns, Joe Hayman, Ted Fields and myself were the most regular customer, of Berry's cafe and we must have drank at least a gallon and a half of Dortmund between us every night.

ctx.x: Other American entertainers in Paris at this time were Opal Cooper who sang at the melody bar just in front of the tabac and Boudons; Snow Fisher, a dancer and drummer; Alberta Hunter, a blues singer; Glover Compton, a singer that accompanied himself on piano; Al Brown the ex-boxing champ; Irene Bullard who had a gymnasium on rue Mansart; Marino and Norris, singers; and Edgar A. Wiggins a journalist for the Chicago Defender, a negro weekly paper. Also Cle Sadler, an alto-sax player; Ray Stokes, pianist; Harry…

Another musician and song writer that I had seen in New York who was now living in Paris was Spencer Williams who composed the famous "Basin Street Blues". I met the members of Willy Lewis's band that were not with him when I met him in the south of France. Joe Hayman played alto-sax and Frank "Big-Boy" Goodie, tenor and clarinet, who was really a big boy about 7 feet tall and must have weighed 280 pounds. He had also played cornet but eventually gave it up. Johnny Mitchell was the guitarist.

I think that Garnet had worked a short while with Willy and it did not go so well because Garnet was quite wild and flighty. So Willy had engaged Herman Chittison whom I had met some years before in Boston accompanying the comedian Stepan Fetchet.
